exact_statement: For every finite-dimensional uniform Boolean sign and fair adaptive physical restriction policy querying each coordinate at most once, with filtration given by past physical observations and an independent policy seed, H(g_t)+sum_{s<t}D_s and I(g_t)+sum_{s<t}d_s are stopped martingales, where D_s=B_s+J_s is the conditional spectral erasure plus the actual physical-child/spectral mutual information and d_s is queried influence. For tau<=n, H(f)=E H(g_tau)+E sum_{s<tau}D_s and I(f)=E I(g_tau)+E sum_{s<tau}d_s.
hypotheses: fair physical queries selected using past only

exact_statement: On every such fair finite tree, lambda_t=sum_{T:b_T^2>0}b_T^2 log2((a_T^2+b_T^2)/b_T^2) satisfies D_t<=lambda_t+(3/ln(2))d_t. Therefore (3/ln(2))I(g_t)-H(g_t)-sum_{s<t}lambda_s is a supermartingale. If at every live node every positive b_T^2/(a_T^2+b_T^2)>=epsilon for fixed epsilon in (0,1], then C I(g_t)-H(g_t) is a supermartingale for C=log2(1/epsilon)+3/ln(2); hence H(f)<=C I(f)+E[H(g_tau)-C I(g_tau)].
hypotheses: same fair finite tree as A061-FAIR-TREE-PROCESS v1
a_T and b_T are actual parent Fourier coefficients without and with queried coordinate
density bound required only for second supermartingale
no universal density or logarithmic payment hypothesis claimed
